The homestand continued with two close games in which the Hoyas completed a regular-season sweep of the series with St. John's in a double-overtime win<ref name=ap20180120>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400988580 Anonymous, "Derrickson's 27 carries Georgetown past St. John's in 2OT," Associated Press, January 20, 2018. Retrieved August 9, 2018]</ref> but then lost to DePaul.<ref name=ap20180124>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400988587 Anonymous, "Cain hits winner as DePaul tops Georgetown 74-73 in thriller," Associated Press, January 24, 2018. Retrieved August 10, 2018]</ref> Marcus Derrickson led the Hoyas against St. John's with 27 points,<ref name=ap20180120/> while Jesse Govan and Jamorko Pickett each scored 16,<ref name=ap20180120/> Jahvon Blair finished with 15 off the bench,<ref name=ap20180120/><ref name=boxscore20180120>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=400988580 St. John's vs. Georgetown  – Box Score – January 20, 2018 – ESPN Retrieved August 9, 2018]</ref> Jagan Moseley came off the bench to contribute 12,<ref name=ap20180120/><ref name=boxscore20180120/> and Trey Dickerson had a double-double (10 points and 11 rebounds);<ref name=ap20180120/> Dickerson scored all of his points in overtime,<ref name=ap20180120/> while Moseley scored seven of his points in the second overtime.<ref name=ap20180120/> In the DePaul game – which the Blue Demons won on the final possession for the second season in a row<ref name=ap20180124/> – Derrickson again led the team with 23 points,<ref name=ap20180124/> Jamorko Pickett had 19 points and eight rebounds,<ref name=ap20180124/> and Moseley finished with 10 off the bench.<ref name=ap20180124/> The Hoyas finished a 1–2 homestand with an overall record of 13–7 and a 3–6 Big East record.

Three road games followed. At Creighton, facing a Bluejays team that was undefeated at home for the season,<ref name=ap20180127>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400988589 Anonymous, "Foster hits 5 3s, scores 28 as Creighton beats Georgetown," Associated Press, January 27, 2018. Retrieved August 9, 2018]</ref> the Hoyas, one of the ten best free-throwing-shooting teams in the United States,<ref name=ap20180127/> shot 16-for-17 (94.1 percent) from the free-throw line,<ref name=ap20180127/> but nonetheless lost 85–77<ref name=ap20180127/> as Creighton went 9-for-10 in free throws over the final 51 seconds;<ref name=ap20180127/> Jahvon Blair scored 21 points<ref name=ap20180127/> and Marcus Derrickson finished with 17.<ref name=ap20180127/> A week later, Georgetown visited No. 6 [[2017–18 Xavier Musketeers men's basketball team|Xavier]], the Hoyas' third game of the season against a ranked opponent,<ref name=ap20180203>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400988598 Anonymous, "Bluiett has 31, No. 6 Xavier beats Georgetown 96-91 in OT," Associated Press, February 3, 2018. Retrieved August 10, 2018]</ref> in a meeting of the Big East's two top rebounding teams.<ref name=ap20180203/> Xavier, the Big East's second-place team,<ref name=ap20180203/> clung to a 46–44 lead at halftime,<ref name=ap20180203/> and the game saw 20 ties and 21 lead changes,<ref name=ap20180203/> with neither team ever leading by more than five points.<ref name=ap20180203/> With 24.3 seconds left in regulation and Georgetown leading 86–82, Jagan Moseley fouled Xavier senior guard [[Trevon Bluiett]] as Bluiett made a three-pointer, and Bluiett sank the resulting free throw to tie the game at 86–86.<ref name=ap20180203/> As time wound down, Jahvon Blair had an open shot<ref name=ap20180203/> that could have won the game but, thinking that the Hoyas should hold the ball for the last shot,<ref name=ap20180203/> passed it up;<ref name=ap20180203/> when he did shoot, attempting a three-pointer with two seconds left to play, he missed badly,<ref name=ap20180203/> and the score stood at 86–86 at the buzzer.<ref name=ap20180203/> In overtime, the Musketeers scored no field goals,<ref name=ap20180203/> but they went 10-for-10 from the free-throw line,<ref name=ap20180203/> and Bluiett – who finished with a season-high 31 points<ref name=ap20180203/> – hit two free throws with 10 seconds left to clinch a 96–91 Xavier victory,<ref name=ap20180203/> the Musketeers′ sixth win in a row.<ref name=ap20180203/> It was Xavier's fourth consecutive defeat of Georgetown<ref name=ap20180203/> and the Musketeers′ seventh win in the past eight meetings between the schools.<ref name=ap20180203/> Jesse Govan, who had posted only 12 points and six rebounds in his last two games combined<ref name=ap20180203/> played a strong inside game in the first half against Xavier,<ref name=ap20180203/> scoring 17 points and grabbing six rebounds before halftime,<ref name=ap20180203/> and he scored 23 points to lead the Hoyas<ref name=ap20180203/> before fouling out early in overtime,<ref name=ap20180203/> while Derrickson had a double-double with 19 points and 15 rebounds;<ref name=ap20180203/> Jamorko Pickett scored 21 points,<ref name=boxscore20180203>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=400988598 Georgetown vs. Xavier – Box Score – February 3, 2018 – ESPN Retrieved August 10, 2018]</ref> and Blair came off the bench to add 19.<ref name=boxscore20180203/> Three days later, the Hoyas′ losing streak reached four when they lost at Providence in a game in which Georgetown led 69-64 with 1:52 remaining but Providence closed out play with a 9–0 scoring run – during which the Friars sank four free throws in the final 4.2 seconds – to win 73–69.<ref name=ap20180207>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400988601 Anonymous, "Providence finishes on 9-0 run to beat Georgetown 73-69," Associated Press, February 7, 2018. Retrieved August 11, 2018]</ref> Govan equaled his career high by finishing with 27 points against the Friars<ref name=ap20180207/> and was the only Hoya to score in double figures,<ref name=boxscore20180206>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=400988601 Georgetown vs. Providence – Box Score – February 6, 2018 – ESPN Retrieved August 10, 2018]</ref> although Derrickson narrowly missed a double-double with nine points and nine rebounds.<ref name=boxscore20180206/> The four consecutive losses dropped Georgetown to 13–10 overall and 3–9 in the Big East.<ref name=ap20180207/>

The Hoyas returned home to meet Seton Hall at Capital One Arena and won their first game in three weeks, despite blowing a 17-point early-second-half lead;<ref name=ap20180210>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400988608 Anonymous, "Georgetown beats Seton Hall after giving away 17-point lead," Associated Press, February 10, 2018. Retrieved August 11, 2018]</ref> the Pirates took their first lead of the game at 69–67 with 5:36 left to play after a 10–0 scoring run,<ref name=ap20180210/> but Marcus Derrickson scored a game-winning deep three-pointer with 4.2 seconds remaining<ref name=ap20180210/> and the Hoyas hung on to win 83–80.<ref name=ap20180210/> Georgetown then traveled to face Butler and won again, snapping a four-game road losing streak.<ref name=ap20180213>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400988610 Anonymous, "Georgetown snaps 4-game road losing streak, tops Butler," Associated Press, February 13, 2018. Retrieved August 11, 2018]</ref> Derrickson had a double-double against the Pirates with 22 points and a career-high 18 rebounds,<ref name=ap20180210/> and against the Bulldogs he scored a career-high 27 points<ref name=ap20180213/> – his eighth 20-plus-point game of the season<ref name=ap20180213/> – on 11-of-13 (84.6 percent) shooting from the field.<ref name=ap20180213/> Jesse Govan scored 11 points against Seton Hall<ref name=ap20180210/> and against Butler had his twelfth double-double of the season with 17 points and 12 rebounds.<ref name=ap20180213/> Jamorko Picket had 18 points against Seton Hall<ref name=ap20180210/> and 10 at Butler,<ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400988610 Georgetown vs. Butler – Box Score – February 13, 2018 – ESPN Retrieved August 10, 2018]</ref> while Trey Dickerson, who was averaging only 3.5 points per game entering the Butler game,<ref name=ap20180213/> came off the bench against the Bulldogs to score a personal-best 12 points in the first half on the way to an 18-point game.<ref name=ap20180213/> It was the first time Georgetown had won consecutive games since the back-to-back victories over North Texas and Alabama A&M in the latter half of December and the Hoyas improved to 15–10 on the season and 5–9 in the conference, but the 2017–2018 Georgetown squad would not win again.

Georgetown's season-ending losing streak began when, after an eight-day break in action, they returned to Capital One Area to begin a three-game homestand with their fourth game of the season against a ranked opponent, a rematch with Xavier, which had climbed to No. 4 in the [[Associated Press Poll]].<ref name=ap20180221>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400988620 Anonymous, "Marshall helps No. 4 Xavier beat Georgetown 89-77," Associated Press, February 21, 2018. Retrieved August 11, 2018]</ref> Georgetown led 40–38 at halftime<ref name=ap20180221/> and still led 50–47 in the second half<ref name=ap20180221/> when Xavier went on a decisive 12–0 scoring run to take a 59–50 lead with 12 minutes left to play.<ref name=ap20180221/> Jamorko Pickett tied a career high with 21 points to lead the Hoyas,<ref name=ap20180221/> sinking a career-high six three-pointers,<ref name=ap20180221/> while Jesse Govan finished with his 13th double-double of the season (18 points and 11 rebounds),<ref name=ap20180221/> Jahvon Blair scored 12 points,<ref name=ap20180221/> and Kaleb Johnson finished with 11,<ref name=ap20180221/> but Xavier outrebounded Georgetown 38–29,<ref name=ap20180221/> including 11–6 in offensive rebounds.<ref name=ap20180221/> Although the Musketeers′ leading scorer, senior guard Trevon Bluiett with 19.8 points per game,<ref name=ap20180221/> scored only two points<ref name=ap20180221/> – giving him a grand total of three points in his last two games at Capital One Arena<ref name=ap20180221/> – Xavier won 89–77,<ref name=ap20180221/> and for the second straight year, the Musketeers swept the season series with the Hoyas.<ref name=ap20180221/> Xavier improved its record to 8–2 against Georgetown since the two schools became charter members of the new Big East Conference in the [[2013–14 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|2013–2014 season]].<ref name=ap20180221/> Georgetown, meanwhile, lost its seventh straight game against Top 25 teams dating back to [[2016–17 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|the previous season]],<ref name=ap20180221/> falling to 0–4 against them for the 2017–2018 season.<ref name=ap20180221/> The loss also guaranteed the Hoyas their third straight losing season in conference play.<ref name=ap20180221/>

The homestand continued with Georgetown losing its eighth straight game to Providence<ref name=ap20180224>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400988625 Anonymous, "Providence tops Georgetown for 8th straight time 74-69," Associated Press, February 24, 2018. Retrieved August 11, 2018]</ref> and losing in overtime to Marquette two days later in a game in which the Hoya defense gave up 18 three-pointers to the Golden Eagles.<ref name=ap20180226>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400988628 Anonymous, "Rowsey scores Marquette's final 9 in OT, downs Georgetown," Associated Press, February 26, 2018. Retrieved August 11, 2018]</ref> Jesse Govan scored the 1,000th point of his collegiate career and had a double-double (20 points and 11 rebounds) against Providence<ref name=ap20180224/> and finished with 25 points, nine rebounds, and five assists against Marquette.<ref name=ap20180226/> Marcus Derrickson had a double-double (11 points and 15 rebounds) against Providence<ref name=ap20180224/> and finished with 15 points in the Marquette game.<ref name=boxscore20180226>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=400988628 Marquette vs. Georgetown – Box Score – February 26, 2018 – ESPN Retrieved August 11, 2018]</ref> Jamorko Pickett scored 12 against Providence,<ref name=boxscore20180224>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=400988625 Providence vs. Georgetown – Box Score – February 24, 2018 – ESPN Retrieved August 11, 2018]</ref> while Jagan Moseley came off the bench to score 12 against the Friars.<ref name=boxscore20180224/> Against the Golden Eagles, Jonathan Mulmore contributed 15 points<ref name=boxscore20180226/> and Jahvon Blair added 16 off the bench.<ref name=boxscore20180226/>

The Hoyas rounded out their regular season with a visit to No. 4 Villanova for their fifth and final game of the season against a ranked opponent.<ref name=ap20180303>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400988637 Anonymous, "Top Cat: Wright wins 413th game as No. 4 Nova tops Hoyas," Associated Press, March 3, 2018. Retrieved August 12, 2018]</ref> Marcus Derrickson, suffering from an injured right ankle, sat out the game.<ref name=ap20180303/> The Hoyas missed all nine of their three-point attempts in the first half<ref name=ap20180303/> and the Wildcats jumped out to a 15-point lead during the half that the Hoyas never really challenged.<ref name=ap20180303/> The teams went into the locker room at halftime with Villanova leading Georgetown 44–31,<ref name=ap20180303/> and Villanova cruised through the second half on the way to a 97–73 victory.<ref name=ap20180303/> The win was [[Jay Wright (basketball)|Jay Wright]]′s 413th as head coach of Villanova, tying him with [[Al Severance]] for the most wins as head coach in the school's history.<ref name=ap20180303/> Jesse Govan shot 10-for-15 from the field and 10-for-10 from the free-throw line to finish with 30 points,<ref name=ap20180303/> and Jamorko Pickett, the only other Hoya to score in double figures, added 10 points.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=400988637 Georgetown vs. Villanova – Box Score – March 3, 2018 – ESPN Retrieved August 12, 2018]</ref> The Hoyas finished in eighth place in the Big East with a conference record of 5–13,<ref name=ap20180303/> the first time they had finished with a losing conference record for three consecutive seasons since [[1997–98 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|1997–1998]], [[1998–99 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|1998–1999]], and [[1999–2000 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|1999–2000]]. They completed the regular season with an overall record of 15–14.<ref name=ap20180303/>

===Big East tournament===
{{main|2018 Big East men's basketball tournament}}

With a No. 8 seed in the [[2018 Big East men's basketball tournament|2018 Big East tournament]] at Madison Square Garden, Georgetown faced ninth-seeded St. John's in the first round. Both schools were charter members of the original Big East Conference when it was created in [[1979–80 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|1979]], and it was their eighth meeting in the tournament since it began in [[1980 Big East men's basketball tournament|1980]];<ref name=ap20180307>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401020063 Anonymous, "St. John's Ponds scores 26 in return from abdominal strain," Associated Press, March 7, 2018. August 13, 2018]</ref> it also was the second straight year that the schools had met in the first round of the [[Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East tournament]].<ref name=ap20180307/> The Hoyas had swept the regular-season series with the Red Storm, but St. John's sophomore point guard [[Shamorie Ponds]], who was the Big East's leading scorer with 26.1 points per game<ref name=ap20180307/> and had averaged 29 points during his last seven games<ref name=ap20180307/> but had missed the Red Storm's final two regular-season games with an abdominal strain,<ref name=ap20180307/> returned to action in time to face the Hoyas.<ref name=ap20180307/> Neither team defended well during the first half,<ref name=ap20180307/> and Georgetown led 48–42 at halftime,<ref name=ap20180307/> but in the second half the Red Storm's defense clamped down, allowing the Hoyas to shoot only 26 percent from the field after halftime.<ref name=ap20180307/> St. John's took the lead for good with an 8–0 scoring run that gave the Red Storm a 67–59 lead with 9:11 left to play.<ref name=ap20180307/> With a balanced attack led by Ponds's 26 points,<ref name=ap20180307/><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=401020063 St. John′s vs. Georgetown – Box Score – March 7, 2018 – ESPN Retrieved August 14, 2018]</ref> St. John's shot 53 percent from the field for the game<ref name=ap20180307/> and the Hoyas never got closer than five points the rest of the way.<ref name=ap20180307/> Winning 88–77,<ref name=ap20180307/> St. John's upset the Hoyas, knocked Georgetown out of the Big East tournament in the first round for the second straight year, and advanced to face Xavier in the quarterfinals.<ref name=ap20180307/> Jesse Govan had a double-double (28 points and 11 rebounds),<ref name=ap20180307/> but scored only eight points in the second half,<ref name=ap20180307/> while Marcus Derrickson returned to action to score 20 points,<ref name=ap20180307/> but the other three Georgetown starters – Jamorko Pickett (two points), Jonathan Mulmore (four points) and Kaleb Johnson, who went scoreless – who were averaging a combined 23.8 points per game for the season entering the Big East tournament,<ref name=ap20180307/> contributed only a total of six points, shooting 1-for-11 (9.1 percent) from the field.<ref name=ap20180307/>

When reporters asked Ewing to reflect on the season in the immediate aftermath of the loss, he replied, "“Right now it's hard to reflect on it. I just have a bitter taste in my mouth right now. So I'm going to take a couple days and reflect. Depending on what happens, see if we're going to get a chance to continue to play and then reflect on it and see — and make that decision. But right now it's hard to say.”<ref name=wallace20180307>[https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/colleges/patrick-ewings-first-season-as-georgetown-coach-ends-with-loss-to-st-johns/2018/03/07/f8fe6b34-2252-11e8-94da-ebf9d112159c_story.html Wallace, Ava, "Patrick Ewing's first season as Georgetown coach ends with loss to St. John's," washingtonpost.com, March 7, 2018 Retrieved August 14, 2018]</ref>

===Wrap-up===

Georgetown's season ended with a five-game losing streak and an overall record of 15–15.<ref name=ap20180307/> For the third straight season, the Hoyas never made the Top 25 in either the [[Associated Press Poll]] or the [[Coaches Poll]] – the first time that had happened in three consecutive seasons since [[1997–98 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|1997-1998]], [[1998–99 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|1998-1999]], and [[1999–2000 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|1999-2000]]. By winning half their games, the Hoyas avoided a third straight losing season, but it nonetheless was the first time Georgetown had three consecutive non-winning seasons since [[1971–72 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|1971–1972]], [[1972–73 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|1972–1973]], and [[1973–74 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|1973–1974]]. Having lost their last five games, nine of their last 11, and 11 of their last 14, the Hoyas were left to hope for a bid to the [[2018 National Invitation Tournament]]<ref name=ap20180307/> – which Ewing said Georgetown would accept<ref name=ap20180307/> – but no invitation came; it was the first time the Hoyas had received an invitation to neither the NCAA Tournament or the NIT in three consecutive seasons since [[1971–72 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|1972]], [[1972–73 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|1973]] and [[1973–74 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|1974]].

Jesse Govan was the team's leading scorer for the year; he started all 30 games, shooting 50.8 percent from the field, averaging 17.9 points and leading the team with 10.0 rebounds per game. Marcus Derrickson started all 29 games he played in, and he averaged 15.9 points and 8.1 rebounds per game, shooting 52.6 percent from the field overall and 46.5 percent from three-point range. Jamorko Pickett played in every game, starting 28 of them, shooting 36.3 percent in field-goal attempts and 35.7 percent from three-point range, and he averaged 9.6 points and 3.8 rebounds per game. Jahvon Blair played in all 30 games and started two of them, averaging 9.0 points per game on 33.2 percent field-goal shooting overall and 32.2 percent from three-point range, and he had 2.2 rebounds per game.  Kaleb Johnson started all 30 games; he ended the season with a field-goal percentage of 54.2 – 34.0 from three-point range – and with per-game averages of 7.9 points and 4.2 rebounds. Jagan Moseley also played in every game and had one start, and he finished with 6.6 points and 2.8 rebounds per game, shooting 48.6 percent from the field and 38.9 percent from beyond the arc. Jonathan Mulmore started 29 of the 30 games he played in, and he averaged 5.6 points per game on 45.9 percent shooting from the field – 46.9 percent in three-point attempts – and grabbed 2.1 rebounds per game. Playing as a reserve in his only season as a Hoya, Trey Dickerson came off the bench in 27 games and averaged 4.4 points and 1.2 rebounds per game, shooting 42.7 percent overall and 27.5 percent in three-pointers. Antwan Walker made one start and came off the bench in 23 other games, averaging 2.7 points and 1.9 rebounds, and shot 49.0 percent from the field overall and 40.0 percent from three-point range. Before his dismissal, Chris Sodom appeared in six games, all as a reserve, and averaged 0.7 point and pulled down an average of 1.3 rebounds per game. Walk-ons Ra'Mond Hines and George Muresan each played in six games.<ref>[https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/schools/georgetown/2018.html sports-reference.com 2017–18 Georgetown Hoyas Roster and Stats Retrieved August 12, 2018]</ref>

Jonathan Mulmore, Trey Dickerson, and Ra'Mond Hines all graduated in 2018. In his two seasons at Georgetown, Mulmore appeared in 62 games, starting 41, shooting 41.2 percent overall from the field and 41.0 percent from three-point range and averaging 4.6 points and 1.7 rebounds per game.<ref>[https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/jonathan-mulmore-1.html sports-reference.com Jonathan Mulmore College stats Retrieved August 12, 2018]</ref> In addition to his only year at Georgetown, Dickerson had played [[2014–15 Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball team|a season at Iowa]] and [[2016–17 South Dakota Coyotes men's basketball team|a season at South Dakota]], and he finished his three-season college career having played in 76 games, starting 34 of them, shooting 40.3 percent from the field and 31.6 percent from three-point range and averaging 6.8 points and 1.5 rebounds per game.<ref>[https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/trey-dickerson-1.html sports-reference.com Trey Dickerson College stats Retrieved August 12, 2018]</ref> Hines, the Hoyas′ one-time student manager, had made the team for two seasons as a walk-on, playing a total of 22 minutes in 11 games, scoring three points and grabbing one rebound.<ref>[https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/ramond-hines-1.html sports-reference.com Ra'Mond Hines College stats Retrieved August 12, 2018]</ref> Also graduating in 2018 was Tre Campbell, who had played guard as a freshman, sophomore, and junior on the Georgetown teams of [[2014–15 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|2014–15]], [[2015–16 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|2015–16]], and [[2016–17 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|2016–17]], then left the team for "personal reasons" in August 2017.<ref name=casualhoya20170809/> He remained enrolled at Georgetown and on scholarship during his senior year, sitting out the 2017-2018 basketball season with a year of college eligibility remaining.<ref name=casualhoya20170809/> He announced on May 8, 2018, that after his graduation from Georgetown he would transfer to [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]] where, as a graduate transfer, he would be eligible to begin play immediately in [[2018–19 South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball team|the 2018-2019 season]].<ref>[https://abcnews4.com/sports/basketball/south-carolina-adds-grad-transfer-campbell-from-georgetown Anonymous, "South Carolina adds grad transfer Campbell from Georgetown," Associated Press, May 8, 2018. Retrieved July 20, 2018]</ref>

Another player who left the team after the season was Marcus Derrickson. Talking to reporters at the end of the season-ending Big East tournament loss to St. John's, he had said he would return to Georgetown to play during his senior year,<ref name=wallace20180307/> but he announced on April 9 that he instead had decided to forego his senior year of college and enter the [[2018 NBA draft]].<ref>[https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/sports/wp/2018/04/09/georgetowns-marcus-derrickson-to-enter-nba-draft/ Wallace, Ava, "Georgetown's Marcus Derrickson to enter NBA draft," washingtonpost.com, April 9, 2018 Retrieved August 12, 2018]</ref> He completed his three-season career at Georgetown having played in 89 games, starting 73 of them, averaging 10.3 points and 5.6 rebounds per game, and shooting 45.9 percent overall from the field and 39.7 percent in three-pointers.<ref>[https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/marcus-derrickson-1.html sports-reference.com Marcus Derrickson College stats Retrieved August 12, 2018]</ref> He went undrafted, but the [[Golden State Warriors]] signed him to play in the [[NBA Summer League]].<ref>[https://www.goldenstateofmind.com/2018/6/22/17493660/2018-nba-draft-undrafted-marcus-derrickson-joins-golden-state-warriors-summer-league-team Anonymous, Klopfer, Brady, "Warriors add Marcus Derrickson to their Summer League team," goldenstateofmind.com, June 22, 2018, 10:12 a.m. PDT Retrieved August 12, 2018]</ref> On April 11, Jesse Govan – who after the season's final game had, like Derrickson, declared an intention to return for his senior year<ref name=wallace20180307/> – announced that he also would not return and would enter the NBA draft,<ref name=wallace20180411>[https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/sports/wp/2018/04/11/georgetowns-jessie-govan-will-test-the-nba-draft-waters/ Wallace, Ava, "Georgetown's Jessie Govan will test the NBA draft waters," washingtonpost.com, April 11, 2018 Retrieved August 12, 2018]</ref> raising the prospect of Georgetown losing two of its most experienced players and its top two scorers. However Govan did not hire an agent and, with his college eligibility therefore still intact,<ref name=wallace20180411/> Georgetown announced on May 24 that he had withdrawn from the draft and would return for his senior year.<ref name=wallace20180524/> Chris Sodom, dismissed from the team in December, decided to transfer to [[George Washington Colonials men's basketball|George Washington]] for [[2018–19 George Washington Colonials men's basketball team|the following season]], a  move which George Washington announced on May 30.<ref>[https://gwsports.com/news/2018/5/30/Sodom_Joins_Men_amp_8217_s_Basketball_Team_.aspx Anonymous, "Sodom Joins Men's Basketball Team," gwsports.com, May 30, 2018, 12:00:00 a.m. EDT Retrieved August 12, 2018]</ref>

When the season ended, Georgetown's RPI stood at 165, below the lowest RPI for a 2018 NCAA Tournament team (16th-seeded [[2017–18 Radford Highlanders men's basketball team|Radford]]′s 128),<ref name=247sports20180308/> and well below the second-lowest RPI in the Big East (Marquette's 58).<ref name=247sports20180308/> The team had played five games against ranked opponents and lost all five of them, the first time Georgetown had not defeated any of its ranked opponents since [[2003-04 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|the 2003–2004 season]].<ref name=ap20180221/> During the season, Georgetown's backcourt had struggled, but the Hoya frontcourt had shown great promise, with Marcus Derrickson, Jesse Govan, and Jamorko Pickett all impressing sports media figures and fans with their offensive prowess. Beginning with the Syracuse game and extending through the Big East season, however, the 2017–18 Hoyas showed a tendency to surrender leads during the second halves of games and "looked nervous and  unprepared in late-game situations;"<ref name=247sports20180308/> in six of its 13 Big East losses, as well as in its non-conference loss to Syracuse, Georgetown had blown a second-half lead.<ref name=247sports20180308/> Its five conference wins had not come easily, either; it had won only one game by more than four points,<ref name=247sports20180308/> its two regular-season wins over ninth-place St. John's had been very close,<ref name=247sports20180308/> and the Hoyas′ wins in conference play seemed "more about Georgetown surviving self-inflicted errors and hanging on for the victory than producing a good effort with solid play from start to finish."<ref name=247sports20180308/> At least some observers blamed Georgetown's non-conference schedule for the team's apparent lack of preparedness for tough late-game situations and frequent inability to hold second-half leads.<ref name=247sports20180308/> They also questioned the optics of Ewing's decision to opt out of the November PK80-Phil Knight Invitational<ref name=247sports20180308/> and the lost opportunity to test the team against marquee opponents and signal Ewing's goal of rebuilding the team to national greatness that the withdrawal represented.<ref name=247sports20180308/> Thus, the season ended as it began, centering around the narrative of the "historically weak" non-conference schedule Ewing had arranged.<ref name=247sports20180308/>

However, the season also ended amid reports that Georgetown had noted the deleterious effects of too weak a schedule both on team preparedness for conference play and on NCAA Tournament selection possibilities and would schedule more challenging opponents for [[2018–19 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|the following season]], including an early-season tournament.<ref name=247sports20180308/><ref>[https://www.casualhoya.com/2018/3/13/17115462/georgetown-hoyas-schedule-non-conference-jamaica-classic-patrick-ewing Anonymous, "Schedule News! Hoyas In The Mix for Non-Conference Tournaments," casualhoya.com, March 13, 2018, 1:13 p.m. EDT. Retrieved July 29, 2018]</ref> With the likelihood of a stronger schedule and of further player development, the return of Jesse Govan, the upcoming eligibility of redshirt senior [[shooting guard]] Greg Malinowski,<ref name=casualhoya20180524>[https://www.casualhoya.com/2018/5/24/17383972/jessie-govan-withdraws-nba-draft-returns-to-georgetown-patrick-ewing Anonymous, "JESSIE's BACK! Jessie Govan to Return to Georgetown," casualhoya.com, May 24, 2018, 8:59 p.m. EDT Retrieved August 12, 2018]</ref> and the anticipated arrival of four highly rated freshman recruits – guard [[Mac McClung]], point guard [[James Akinjo]], and forwards Josh LeBlanc and Grayson Carter<ref name=casualhoya20180524/> – sports pundits even saw a possibility of Georgetown returning to the NCAA Tournament in [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2019]].<ref name=247sports20180308/>
